result.title: Conservative Dueling Bandits: Preference Learning under Baseline Constraints
result.summary: Contextual dueling bandits learn from pairwise comparisons, the same feedback used to fine-tune language models from human preferences. Standard algorithms explore aggressively and can show users two poor options. We study conservative contextual dueling bandits, which require that, at every round, the cumulative score of the better displayed item stay above a $(1-α)$ fraction of a trusted baseline's. An item's score is its probability of beating the best available item, so the constraint depends only on utility differences and needs no absolute rewards. This also changes how safety can be certified: we show that transferring the safety test of the conservative bandit algorithm CLUCB unchanged can incur linear regret, even when the baseline's utilities are known exactly. For linear utilities, we develop MaxInP-BC, which certifies scores through utility gaps and, when it must fall back, pairs the baseline with an informative partner so that fallback rounds still drive learning. It is safe with high probability at all times, with regret $\tilde{O}(d\sqrt{T}/κ)$ plus an additive cost of conservatism that does not grow with the horizon. For general utility classes, we develop BTIGW-BC, which turns the guarantee of an online logistic-regression oracle into cumulative safety certificates. It is safe at all times, makes finitely many fallbacks, and has sublinear regret whenever the oracle's logistic regret is sublinear. In experiments, both satisfy the constraint, which their unconstrained counterparts often violate, at a moderate cost in regret.

AI.brief_summary: 研究带保守约束的情境化对决老虎机：要求每轮较优展示项的累积得分不低于可信基线的 (1-α) 比例，证明直接沿用 CLUCB 的安全检验会产生线性遗憾，并提出 MaxInP-BC（线性效用）与 BTIGW-BC（一般效用类）两类算法，给出任意时刻高概率安全与次线性遗憾保证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其仅依赖效用差（相对偏好）定义安全约束、以及在回退时搭配「信息量大的对手」以继续学习的思路，可能为 VLM 偏好式训练中的受限监督与比较样本分配提供概念线索，但论文不含 latent 状态或视觉证据机制，需较多核查。
